utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. Madam Registrar, please call the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-67-R77.1-PT, contempt case against Ljubisa Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to welcome the accused as well as his temporarily assigned counsel, Ms. Branislava Isailovic. Welcome to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have technical problems? I can see that there is a problem, but it has been solved. Mr. Petkovic, can you hear the translation of what is being said in the courtroom in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies. Yes, I do have -- I am receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pursuant to Rule 65 bis (A) of the Rules, a Trial Chamber or a Trial Chamber Judge shall convene a Status Conference within 120 days of the initial appearance of the accused, and its aim is to organize exchanges between the parties so as to ensure expeditious preparation for trial. I'd like to add that it is in the interests of justice to do our utmost so that this trial can be conducted as soon as possible. This Status Conference also gives an opportunity to review the status of the case and to allow the accused the opportunity to raise issues thereto, including his health condition. Are you listening to me, Mr. Petkovic? Is everything so far clear?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Judge Lattanzi, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given that Mr. Petkovic is charged with only one count, it was deemed appropriate to convene this Status Conference well before the expiry of the dead-line, and right after the assignment of Ms. Isailovic by the Registrar. We have so decided in order to conduct a very expeditious trial. I'd like to turn to the Defence counsel. Ms. Isailovic, have you received all the materials which had been disclosed to the duty counsel in this case? Have you received everything so far?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe I have received almost everything from my predecessor, Mr. Guy-Smith. I have received the materials that were disclosed to him upon his the request by the Prosecutor. I have received all these materials. But given the fact that I was assigned very recently, I was in Paris yesterday, I was very busy because of the upcoming vacation. However, while I was in the train, I have managed to review all the materials, and it seems to me that the latest summons was dated -- which was dated end of April was not amongst the materials that were given to me. My client has disclosed his case-related materials, but they're drafted in Serbian but I would like to have them in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because it's working language at the Tribunal, therefore, you'd like to have them in French. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this latest summons dated April 2008, as well as the notification of delivery, is missed from my file. I don't have them. But in due time, I will turn to the Prosecutor or the registry to have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will do our best to make sure that you receive those materials in the afternoon. After having received these materials, do you think that disclosure will be completed?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I believe that after I've received those materials, disclosure will be completed. I would like to inform you that I intend to file a motion for provisional release as soon as possible. I have seen the dates for court recess. Court recess is supposed to start on the 25th of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And court recess will finish mid-August, so I intend to file this motion as soon as possible, possibly by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I must say that I'm very happy that you're speaking French. This makes life easier for me. During the initial appearance, we were informed by the duty counsel that 45 days might be necessary for the preparation of this case. What is your position in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I haven't received that information, maybe my colleague forgot to mention it, but it seems to me that this is a reasonable dead-line. I've had experience with another contempt case before this Tribunal, and it seems appropriate. The proceedings in contempt cases are not as complex in -- as in other cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, you confirmed that this time-period will be sufficient for the preparation of this case. Very well. Can you already give us an indication as to the number of witnesses that you intend to call, even though it might be a little too early. But maybe you already know how many witnesses you intend to call, as well as the number of courtroom hours which you wish to use in this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it might be a little presumptuous to give you an indication now, given the fact that I was assigned to this case very recently. However, in view of my experience in similar cases, I believe that a few witnesses, between three and five witnesses, would be called. For the time being, I don't know exactly what the Defence case will be. Not everything has been decided. So maybe I can tell you at a later stage how many exhibits, how many witnesses will be used. However, I can tell you already that I will do my best to be brief. I'll be brief. I was temporarily assigned to this case, but we have to act quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We have to do our utmost in order to conduct an expeditious trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree with you. In the course of July, I think we'll be able to tell you more precisely what we intend to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, you know how to contact the Legal Officer of the Chamber. If need be, you can contact her. You can ask her the necessary information at the end of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think this will be very useful. I believe that we will cooperate in a very effective manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petkovic, do you have any issues to raise as to the conditions of your detention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Honourable Judge Lattanzi, I have never been in prison or in detention so far, and I cannot tell what the situation in other detention units is. As for the Detention Unit I'm presently -- I'm currently in, I can only say things that are commendable for the UNDU staff. I don't know what else I could say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we move into private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Isailovic, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you, Your Honour. I believe that for now all the topics on the agenda have been dealt with. I would like to add, once again, that I'm quite concerned about the fact that I was assigned provisionally. I explained to Mr. Petkovic and I believe that he understood, but maybe you can confirm this, that the procedure can be very short, before actually the registry checks the situation of the other counsel. I believe that Mr. Petkovic understood this and that he now agrees with my temporary assignment because I can't just wait. You know, I'm a lawyer, I work at the French bar, a prestigious bar. That doesn't mean, of course, that other bars aren't as prestigious Paris. But in Paris, our code of ethics is sacred, and I'll do everything I can, of course, for my client, even though I was only assigned temporarily. So it might be wise maybe to make sure that Mr. Petkovic had fully understood this. This will be quite reassuring for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petkovic, I'm sure you've heard what Mrs. Isailovic just said, your temporary counsel. Would you like to add anything or would you comment on this? You agree with her approach?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I absolutely agree, and I'm quite certain that we will complete all the necessary formalities during next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mrs. Isailovic, I wanted you to know that you will be kept informed in due time of other Status Conferences that might be organized if need be.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for this. I apologise. I'd forgotten to turn on the microphone. I took note of what you just told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If there's no other items on the agenda, I believe that we can adjourn this hearing. I'd like to thank everyone and see you next time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: adjourned at 2.50 p.m.
